gaps.sentence: After years of setbacks, the tunnel was ___ completed in 2019.
gaps.explanation: 'Eventually' = in the end, after a long delay or difficulty.

gaps.sentence: ___ I thoroughly enjoyed the novel, the sequel left me cold.
gaps.explanation: Concessive 'while' = although, introducing the clause of concession.

gaps.sentence: ___ the weather improves, the crossing will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: Unless = if the weather doesn't improve — matching the cancellation.
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.

gaps.sentence: You can stay up late tonight ___ it's a school night tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless it's a school night' = if it isn't a school night.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: Please complete the form in block capitals ___ it can be read easily.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces a clause with subject and modal; so as to/in order to need an infinitive.
